resources.string: Setup
Execution
Instructions for this exercise are not available in this version. Follow your own setup and technique, and use a load you can control.
Close
Lie on the bench with your eyes beneath the bar. Plant both feet, settle your upper back on the pad, and take an even grip just wider than shoulder width. Unrack the bar with your arms extended.

Lower the bar under control toward the middle of your chest, keeping your wrists over your elbows. Touch lightly without bouncing, then press up until your arms are extended. Keep your shoulders settled against the bench.

Sit on the bench with a dumbbell in each hand, then lie back and hold them beside your chest. Plant both feet and keep your upper back supported. Turn your palms forward or slightly inward, whichever feels comfortable.

Press both dumbbells upward over your chest without letting them collide. Lower them under control until your elbows are beside or slightly below your torso, within a comfortable range. Keep both sides moving smoothly.

Place your hands on the floor a little wider than shoulder width and extend your legs behind you. Brace your trunk so your head, hips and legs form a steady line. Use an elevated hand support if needed to make the movement manageable.

Bend your elbows and lower your chest between your hands while keeping your body in one line. Stop at a comfortable depth, then press the floor away to return to the start. Avoid letting your hips sag or rise ahead of your shoulders.
Stand with the bar at your upper chest and take a balanced grip just outside your shoulders. Set your feet comfortably, keep your trunk steady, and position your elbows slightly in front of the bar.

Press the bar overhead in a controlled path, moving your head clear as the bar passes. Finish with the bar balanced over your shoulders and feet, without forcing your lower back to arch. Lower it smoothly to your upper chest.
Hold a dumbbell in one hand and support yourself with the other hand on a stable bench or surface. Set your feet securely and keep your back steady, with the working arm hanging below your shoulder.

Draw the dumbbell toward your hip, keeping your elbow close to your side. Pause briefly without twisting your torso, then lower the weight until your arm is extended. Complete the repetitions on one side before switching.

Sit facing the cable station and secure your thighs beneath the pads. Take the bar with an even, comfortable overhand grip. Sit tall and let your arms extend overhead without losing a steady torso position.

Pull the bar down toward your upper chest while keeping your torso mostly upright and your elbows moving down. Return the bar overhead slowly until your arms extend comfortably. Do not swing or pull the bar behind your neck.
Sit facing the cable station with feet on the supports and knees slightly bent. Take the handle with both hands and sit tall, allowing your arms to reach forward while keeping your torso steady.

Draw the handle toward your lower ribs, moving your elbows back without leaning to create momentum. Briefly settle your shoulder blades, then let the cable carry your hands forward under control while maintaining your seated position.
Stand with a dumbbell in each hand beside your thighs. Keep a soft bend in your elbows and choose a load you can lift without swinging. Set your feet comfortably and keep your torso steady.

Raise your arms out to the sides in a smooth arc, leading with your elbows. Stop around shoulder height or sooner if that is your comfortable range. Lower the dumbbells slowly; avoid shrugging or using momentum.

Set the bar securely across your upper back and take an even grip. Stand with your feet about shoulder width apart, or in a stance that lets you squat comfortably. Brace your trunk and make sure the bar is stable before stepping back.

Bend your hips and knees together, keeping your whole foot in contact with the floor. Descend only as far as you can maintain a steady position, then stand by pushing through the floor. Keep the bar balanced over your mid-foot.

Hold one dumbbell vertically close to your chest with both hands supporting it. Stand with your feet in a comfortable squat stance and brace your trunk. Keep the weight close rather than letting your arms drift forward.

Bend your hips and knees to lower between your legs while keeping the weight close to your chest. Use a depth where your balance and torso remain controlled, then stand smoothly. Keep your feet grounded throughout.
Stand with a barbell held in front of your thighs and feet about hip width apart. Keep your knees softly bent, arms long and trunk braced. Begin with the bar close to your body.

Push your hips back and let the bar slide close down your thighs and shins. Keep your back steady and knees softly bent; stop when your hamstrings limit the hinge or your position would change. Drive your hips forward to stand tall without leaning back.

Adjust the machine so its pivot is near your knee and the roller rests comfortably against the backs of your lower legs. Set the seat and supports, then hold the handles with your hips supported against the pad.

Bend your knees to draw the roller through a comfortable range without lifting your hips. Pause briefly, then extend your legs slowly until they return to the starting position. Keep the movement smooth rather than letting the stack drop.
Stand with a dumbbell in each hand, arms by your sides and palms facing forward or slightly inward. Keep your feet steady, shoulders relaxed and elbows near your torso.

Bend your elbows to curl the dumbbells toward your shoulders without rocking your torso. Keep your upper arms mostly still, then lower the weights under control until your arms are extended comfortably.
Stand facing the cable with the attachment set around chest height. Hold it with both hands, elbows bent and close to your sides. Set your feet securely and keep your torso steady.

Straighten your elbows to press the attachment down while keeping your upper arms near your sides. Finish in a comfortable extension, then bend your elbows slowly to return. Avoid leaning your body onto the handle.
Stand on a level floor with a dumbbell in each hand beside your thighs. Set your feet about hip width apart and keep your knees softly extended. Choose a load that lets you balance without rocking.

Press through the balls of your feet to raise your heels while keeping your torso steady. Pause briefly, then lower your heels to the floor under control. Keep the dumbbells beside your body and avoid bouncing.

Adjust the standing calf raise machine so the shoulder pads rest comfortably on your shoulders. Select or rack the load according to the machine, then stand with the balls of your feet on its platform and hold the handles. Lift into a steady position and release the safety catch if present.

Raise your heels by pressing through the balls of your feet, keeping your knees softly extended and your torso steady. Pause briefly, then lower your heels through a comfortable range without bouncing. Re-engage the safety catch if present before stepping off.
Hold a pull-up bar with a secure, comfortable grip and let your body hang without swinging. Keep your shoulders controlled and legs together, with knees straight or softly bent as needed.

Lift your legs by bringing your thighs toward your torso without building momentum. Raise only through a range you can control, then lower slowly until your body is still. Bend your knees if that helps maintain control.
